title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
subject: psychiatry
summary: Suspect NMS with fever, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability and raised CK after a dopamine antagonist or withdrawal of dopaminergic drugs. Stop the causative drug at once, give intensive supportive care with cooling and fluids, benzodiazepines, and dantrolene and/or bromocriptine for moderate to severe cases; ECT if refractory.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Follows exposure to a dopamine antagonist (typical or atypical antipsychotic, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine), usually within the first 2 weeks of starting or increasing it, or withdrawal of levodopa or other dopaminergic drugs.

Core features (international consensus, DSM-5): hyperthermia above 38°C on at least 2 occasions, severe (lead-pipe) rigidity, altered mental status (delirium, stupor, mutism), and CK at least 4 times the upper limit of normal.
Autonomic instability: tachycardia (25% or more above baseline), raised or fluctuating BP, profuse sweating, urinary incontinence, pallor, tachypnoea (50% or more above baseline).
Develops over 1 to 3 days; rigidity and mental status change often precede fever. Atypical antipsychotics can cause milder or incomplete forms.
Risk factors: high doses, rapid dose increases, parenteral or depot antipsychotics, dehydration, agitation, catatonia and previous NMS.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CK (usually above 600 IU/L, often much higher), CBC (leukocytosis), renal function, electrolytes including calcium, magnesium and phosphate, liver function, urine myoglobin, coagulation and blood gas.

Exclude mimics: sepsis, meningitis or encephalitis (lumbar puncture if uncertain), heat stroke, serotonin toxicity, malignant catatonia, anticholinergic toxicity, thyrotoxicosis, and autoimmune (anti-NMDA receptor) encephalitis.
CT or MRI brain when the diagnosis is unclear or there are focal signs.

sections.title: Immediate management
items: Stop the antipsychotic and any other dopamine antagonist immediately on suspicion; do not wait for CK. If caused by stopping levodopa, restart it.
HDU or ICU for moderate to severe cases. Cool actively (cool room at 21 to 23°C, cooling blankets, ice packs) and give IV fluids to correct dehydration and protect the kidneys from myoglobin.
Protect the airway: intubate for reduced consciousness, dysphagia with aspiration risk, or respiratory muscle rigidity. Aspiration pneumonia and AKI are the main complications.
VTE prophylaxis, pressure-area care and nutrition.

sections.title: Drug treatment
items: Benzodiazepines for mild cases and for agitation or catatonic features: for example lorazepam 1 to 2 mg IV or IM every 4 to 6 hours.
Dantrolene for marked rigidity and hyperthermia: 1 to 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated as needed up to 10 mg/kg/day; oral dantrolene can follow as the patient improves. Monitor liver function.

Bromocriptine (dopamine agonist): 2.5 mg orally or via nasogastric tube three times daily, increased by 2.5 to 7.5 mg/day as needed to a maximum of 45 mg/day. It can cause vomiting, hypotension and worsening psychosis.
Dantrolene and bromocriptine can be combined in severe cases; evidence comes from case series and expert consensus only. Taper slowly after recovery to avoid relapse.
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for NMS not responding to drug treatment or with persistent catatonia.
Do not use dantrolene or bromocriptine for serotonin toxicity; distinguish the two carefully.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Core temperature, heart rate, BP, respiratory rate, SpO2 and urine output closely; CK, creatinine and potassium at least daily.
Watch for AKI from myoglobinuria, aspiration pneumonia, DIC, venous thromboembolism, arrhythmias and stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy.
With treatment NMS usually resolves over 3 to 14 days (longer after depot antipsychotics); mortality is around 10%.

sections.title: Restarting antipsychotics
items: Wait at least 2 weeks after full recovery before any rechallenge, and avoid re-using the same drug.
Choose a lower-potency antipsychotic, start low and titrate slowly, avoid parenteral and depot preparations, keep the patient well hydrated, and monitor temperature, rigidity and CK.
One episode increases the risk of another: document NMS clearly as an adverse reaction and consider ECT as an alternative treatment for the psychiatric illness.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving more antipsychotic (for example IM haloperidol for agitation) to a febrile, rigid, confused patient.
Treating as sepsis alone without stopping the antipsychotic.
Missing NMS with atypical antipsychotics, where fever and rigidity may be less marked.
Early rechallenge with the same antipsychotic.

drugs.name: Dantrolene
drugs.dose: 1 to 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeat as needed up to 10 mg/kg/day
drugs.notes: Severe rigidity and hyperthermia; hepatotoxicity with prolonged use.

drugs.name: Bromocriptine
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg orally or via nasogastric tube three times daily; increase by 2.5 to 7.5 mg/day to a maximum of 45 mg/day
drugs.notes: May worsen psychosis; watch BP and vomiting.

drugs.name: Lorazepam
drugs.dose: 1 to 2 mg IV or IM every 4 to 6 hours
